newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Caspian says ups Brazil in LatAm stock portfolio.
newsitem.headline: Caspian says ups Brazil in LatAm stock portfolio.

text.p: Caspian Securities said it raised Brazil's weighting to 49 percent from 47 percent in its model Latin American stocks portfolio.

"We are increasing our asset allocation for Brazil to 49 percent from 47 percent and recommend that investors take advantage of the recent stock market correction to increase their weightings," it said in its daily report.
Caspian said Brazil still offers the best value in Latin America and is still at a relatively early stage of reform.

It said it does not believe that the market had discounted upcoming key events which should have a beneficial impact, such as the conclusion of the Band B cellular selloff, privatizations in the telecom, power and banking sectors, civil service and pension reforms and the likely re-election of President Fernando Henrique Cardoso in 1998.
According to Caspian, the market's recent weakness has been due to domestic mutual fund redemptions and not foreign selling.
"We expect mutual fund redemptions to taper off shortly and net inflows to resume in the second quarter of 1997," it said.
Currently, only 13.4 percent of the 140 billion reais of mutual funds are in equity securities, Caspian said.
"We believe that given the stable economic environment and lower real interest rates, equity weightings in domestic mutual funds will rise to 20 percent of total assets by year's end," it added.
Caspian also said it expects foreign inflows into Latin America to remain strong. It said inflows into Latin American mutual funds reached their highest weekly level since the Mexican crisis in 1994.
Inflows are driven by strong economic fundamentals and attractive equity valuations, it said.
While Caspian raised Brazil to 49 percent, it cut Peru to 2.0 percent from 3.0 percent and Colombia to 1.0 percent from 2.0 percent.
It remains overweight in Mexico, Venezuela and Brazil, and underweight in Argentina, Chile, Colombia and Peru.
